Enter Agentic AI: What It Is (And Isn’t)

Agentic AI refers to intelligent software agents that pursue goals, learn from context, and take action — often independently. Think of them as tireless digital team members who don’t just follow rules. They interpret your goals, adapt to changing inputs, and execute tasks based on real-world data.
What sets them apart from traditional automation or
is their autonomy and flexibility. You don’t need to spell out every step.

For example, a CFO might instruct the agent to "reconcile intercompany accounts," and the agent determines how to get it done. If a new entity is added or unexpected data appears, the agent can adjust without breaking, unlike rigid macros.

Many are powered by language models, which means they can communicate in natural language, answering questions, flagging anomalies, or even generating narrative reports that explain performance in plain English.

This isn’t about replacing finance professionals. It’s about removing the repetitive, manual work that holds them back. With agentic AI, teams can focus on higher-level tasks: interpreting results, modeling future scenarios, and advising the business.

Agentic AI is transforming financial consolidation from a tedious, manual chore into a streamlined, intelligent process. Here's a breakdown of how it works in practice:

Once data is standardized, agents scan intercompany transactions across subsidiaries. They identify matches, flag discrepancies, and reconcile balances in real time. Human intervention is only needed when exceptions arise, significantly reducing the hours spent chasing down mismatches.

With data aligned and reconciled, agents apply consolidation rules such as ownership percentages, intercompany eliminations, and foreign currency adjustments. These actions happen dynamically and continuously, so financials stay up to date throughout the period, not just at month-end.

Together, these capabilities shorten the close cycle, reduce errors, and allow finance teams to shift their focus from compiling data to delivering high-value insights.
A CFO’s Roadmap to AI-Driven Consolidation

Adopting agentic AI in finance isn’t about flipping a switch. It’s a strategic, phased transformation that starts with foundational readiness and grows into scalable impact. For CFOs looking to modernize consolidation processes and unlock real-time financial intelligence, the journey begins with a few critical steps:

AI is only as effective as the data it works with. Standardize your Chart of Accounts, unify entity mappings, and ensure consistent tagging of intercompany transactions. Clean data reduces friction and accelerates automation readiness.

Don’t try to automate everything at once. Begin with a pilot project, such as reconciling a high-volume intercompany account or automating a specific elimination scenario. This creates a quick win and builds internal momentum.

Build trust by embedding governance into the process. Establish review checkpoints, implement audit trails, and prepare exception-handling protocols. This ensures transparency and maintains compliance even as automation increases.

Equip your finance professionals to work effectively with AI. Focus on developing skills for reviewing, validating, and interpreting AI-generated outputs. The goal is to empower your team to lead with insights, not just transactions.
Once your data, team, and systems are aligned, expand automation to more entities, accounts, and reporting workflows. With each stage, agentic AI adds speed, accuracy, and strategic value.

By following this roadmap, CFOs can lead their organizations into a future where consolidation is continuous, insights are real-time, and finance plays a more proactive role in decision-making. The earlier the investment, the greater the competitive edge.
